To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electronic properties of the substrate surface states are hardly modified by graphene nanoflaks, whereas the electronic properties of nanoflakes are strongly influenced by the metal substrate.
graphene nanoflaks on Ag(111), Au(111) are weakly coupled to the underlying metal surface.

graphene nanoflakers on Au(111), Ag(111) surfaces exhibit a linear dispersion relation around the Fermi energy and that the doping level is larger on Ag(111), which is in agreement with DFT calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electronic and structural properties of graphene nanosheets on Au(111), Ag(111), Cu(111), and Pt(111) substrates.
the electronic structure of graphene nanoflake on Ag(111), which has not been studied before, and the comparison of the graphene/Ag(11) and graphene/Au(11) systems.
the structural and electronic properties of single-layer graphene nanoflakers (GNFLs) on Ag(111).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electronic structure of graphene is only weakly perturbed by the metal substrate.

the interaction between graphene and Ag(111), Au(111) is rather weak and that the electronic structure of graphene is preserved in the nanoflakes, with the Fermi level shifted to higher (Au(111)) or lower energies (Ag(111)), depending on the substrate.
the electronic properties of the graphene nanoflaks are mainly governed by the interaction between the nanoflakes themselves, with a minor contribution from the underlying metal surface.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the interaction between graphene and Au(111), as well as Ag(111) surfaces is rather weak and the electronic structure of graphene nanoflake is only slightly modified by the substrate, with the Fermi level of the graphene nanoflake being slightly p-doped for graphene/Au and n-doped for graphene/Ag.
the electronic properties of the graphene nanoflake can be described as a hybridization of the graphene and the substrate surface states.
the interaction between graphene and Ag(111)/Au(111) is rather weak.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the graphene nanoflake/substrate system can be described as a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) with a parabolic dispersion relation for the substrate-derived surface states and a linear dispersion relation for the graphene-derived states.

the interaction between graphene and Ag(111)/Au(111) is rather weak, and the electronic properties of the nanoflakes can be described by the tight-binding model of graphene with a slight doping and a small renormalization of the Fermi velocity.
the electronic properties of single graphene nanoflake are well described in the framework of DFT-D2 and DFT-D3 approaches.
